statement: You are given an integer array nums. A subsequence keeps some of the elements in their original order, and it is strictly increasing if each element is larger than the one before it.
Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of nums, in O(n log n) time.

The usual method keeps a sorted list tails, where tails[k] is the smallest value that can end an increasing subsequence of length k + 1. Each element either extends tails or replaces the first entry that is ≥ it, found by binary search, and the final size of tails is the answer.

examples.explanation: tails ends as [2, 3, 7, 18]. Its size, 4, is the length of the longest increasing subsequence.
Every element is smaller than the one before, so each one replaces the only entry and tails never grows past size 1.
